title: Remove the leftover price-label adhesive from a returned pan's base with a 91% IPA wipe
instruction: Remove the leftover price-label adhesive from the pan's base, and leave it clean and dry.
context: Almost everyone has pulled a price label off a new hard-anodized pan and tried to get the glue off without damaging the dark finish. In retail returns, stockers and order fillers (2,764,800 US jobs, SOC 53-7065) and retail salespersons (3,936,700, SOC 41-2031) clean returned merchandise before it goes back on the shelf (BLS National Employment Matrix, 2024). The label's permanent pressure-sensitive adhesive is a thin film: 91% isopropyl alcohol swells it, a lint-free Chempad lifts it, and a dry or gritty pad can burnish or scratch the anodized surface. The setup is not a stand-in: a real 12-inch Calphalon Premier pan, a real Avery 5163 label and real Chemtronics Chempads. The instruction states only the goal; the wet, dwell, wipe and fresh final pad are the robot's to choose.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0.7475. A 310 x 310 x 3 mm high-friction silicone mat is fixed at x 0.270, y 0, its top at z 0.7505. The real Calphalon Premier 12-inch pan, 0.305 m across and 1.63 kg, is upside down on the mat, centred at x 0.270, y 0; its rim ring rests on the mat and its base face is up at z 0.8145. Its stainless handle, 0.20 m long, 25 mm wide and 15 mm thick, points to the robot's left (+y) from y 0.147 to 0.347, centred at z 0.786; the left hand grips the mounting collar. The pan is free, not clamped. An 80 x 40 mm Avery 5163 adhesive patch, divided into 128 cells of 5 mm (8 across x, 16 along y), is centred on the base; a small holder of 128 thin pale cell plates follows the pan and hides each cell 0.3 mm inside the base when it is clean. The peeled 80 x 40 mm white label lies on the waste tray at x 0.460, y -0.180, with its blue TrueBlock strip. A 260 x 220 x 20 mm tool/pad tray is fixed at x 0.280, y -0.290; on it are three opened foil packets at x 0.180, 0.260 and 0.340, y -0.300, each carrying a Chemtronics Chempad (76 x 102 mm, 3 mm felt) on a backing foot with a 30 mm round grip bar. A 140 x 120 x 20 mm waste tray is fixed at x 0.480, y -0.220. A 120 x 120 mm clear 5 mm grid overlay and a 10x loupe are on the bench at x 0.470, y 0.330 and x 0.520, y 0.270. A 30-degree raking LED stands at x 0.520, y -0.060, its head aimed at the pan base. The two YAM arms start at READY; the left hand grips the pan handle and the right hand works the pads.
scoring: The scored state is the 5 mm cell patch on the pan base. Each of the 128 cells starts at residue 1.0; a cell is clean when its residue is <= 0.01. A pad places and wets the patch when it is within 20 degrees of flat, at 0.5 N or more, the left hand holds the pan, and the pad's 76 x 102 mm face is over the patch: that is 0.25. A cell is removed only while a pad is in real contact with the base: the live scorer sums the normal force from the contact solver (MuJoCo locally, PhysX on Isaac) and subtracts 0.20 of residue per mm of pad rubbing on a soft cell, 0.08/mm on a wet cell and 0.02/mm on a dry cell; a pad above the base, or moving beside the patch, removes nothing. Twenty seconds of wet contact (the real protocol is 30 s) makes the cells soft; the surface film dries 6 s after the pad lifts and the swollen adhesive stays soft for 45 s. The score is 0.5 at 60% of the cells clean, 0.75 at 90% with the fresh white final pad, and 1.0 at 98% (126/128) plus a fresh white final pad (not used for the dwell, load <= 0.05 g, used for the final wipe), a dry base (surface IPA <= 0.05), no scratch and no residue outside the 80 x 40 mm patch, with the state held 1 s and the right tool off the pan. Idle is 0. A dirty pad (load above 0.05 g) redeposits a 0.12 film and caps the result at 0.5; residue outside the patch is 0; a gritty pad that rubs latches a scratch and scores 0; a pan off the mat is 0. The ladder is 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0. Real checks: a phone photo through the 5 mm grid for the before/after cells, the white final Chempad, a 10x loupe, a dry white wipe and a 30-degree raking light for a bright scratch line. There is no gloss meter. The video shows the 1 s hold.
reset_notes: Wash and dry the pan base; wipe it with a fresh Chempad and let it dry 30 s. Apply one 80 x 40 mm piece cut from an Avery 5163 label with a card jig, press it with a 2 kg roller (three passes), age 24 h at 23 C / 50% RH, then peel it at 180 degrees at about 300 mm/s in one steady pull; put the facestock on the waste tray and do not rub the residue. Photograph the base through the 5 mm grid and mark every residue cell; the sim starts with 128 cells. Place the pan upside down at x 0.270, y 0 on the mat; handle to the robot's left. Put a fresh Chempad on each of the three foil packets and the peeled label on the waste tray. The arms start at READY. Use a fresh working pad and a fresh white final pad each trial.
fidelity: Real: Calphalon pan 1.63 kg, 30.5 cm; Avery 5163 label 80 x 40 mm; Chemtronics Chempad 76 x 102 mm, 91% IPA. Sim: pan 0.305 m, 1.63 kg; 128 cells of 5 mm on the 80 x 40 mm patch; pad 76 x 102 x 3 mm, 0.045 kg, compliant 900 N/m, wet felt friction 0.55/0.45 (EST); removal only by pad contact force and rubbing distance: 0.20/mm soft, 0.08/mm wet, 0.02/mm dry; 20 s sim dwell vs 30 s real; 6 s surface dry, 45 s soft; 98% cell threshold; no gloss meter.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the policy never picks a pad; the video replays that run's 2,400 recorded actions because the original frame store was deleted). Demo: 1.0 at step 1,446 on Isaac (PhysX contact) and MuJoCo. Pytest 13.
